title: Greetings from the Rainforest
text:
Dear Uncle Ben,

Hello from the rainforest! It rained {number} times today, and every drop was as big as a {noun}. Our guide, Rosa, showed us a tiny frog that was bright {color}. She says it sings {adverb} every night to call its friends.

Yesterday we crossed a rope bridge over a little stream. A monkey sat in the middle and would not move until I gave him my {plural noun}. Then he {past tense verb} and swung away.

Our hotel is a treehouse. My bed is a {adjective} hammock, and a parrot outside my window says "{silly word}" every morning. Tomorrow we are going to {verb} down the river in a canoe. I hope I see a sloth {verb ending in ing}!

Your nephew,
Sam

title: What to Pack for the Jungle
text:
Going on a jungle trip? Here is what every explorer needs to pack.

First, bring a raincoat and a pair of {adjective} boots. The jungle is very muddy, and the mud likes to {verb}. Next, pack a flashlight, a water bottle, and {number} {plural noun}. You never know when you might need them.

Do not forget bug spray! The jungle mosquitoes are small but very {adjective}. My cousin forgot his bug spray last year, and he {past tense verb} the whole week. You should also bring a snack to share with your group. The monkeys are not allowed to have {food}, but they will ask {adverb} anyway.

Last of all, pack a notebook so you can draw every {noun} you see. Happy {verb ending in ing}!

title: Explorer's Journal, Day Three
text:
Day three in the jungle. I woke up at sunrise because a toucan was {verb ending in ing} on my tent. I gave him a {noun}, and he flew away happy.

After breakfast, Professor Plum and I hiked to the Great Waterfall. On the way, we found a giant flower that smelled exactly like {food}. Professor Plum wrote it down in her {adjective} notebook.

At the waterfall, we saw a family of monkeys taking a bath. The baby monkey {past tense verb} so {adverb} that we all started laughing. Then he tossed {number} {plural noun} into the water.

Tonight we are camping by the river. Professor Plum says the frogs here can {verb} better than any frog in the world. I am trying to stay awake to hear them, but I am very {adjective}. Tomorrow we will look for the rare purple {noun}.

title: Jungle News: The Big Parrot Parade
text:
This is Jungle Radio with today's top story.

The Big Parrot Parade happened this morning by the river. More than {number} parrots marched in a line, each one wearing a tiny {noun} on its head. The parade was led by Captain Feathers, the oldest parrot in the jungle. He flew {adverb} at the front and shouted "{exclamation}!" every few minutes.

Next came the toucans, who played the drums with their {plural noun}. A group of frogs followed, {verb ending in ing} as loudly as they could. "This is the most {adjective} parade we have ever had," said Mrs. Leaf, a tree frog who watched from a branch. "I hope next year they will {verb} even more."

The parade ended at the big mango tree, where everyone shared {plural noun} and {past tense verb} until sunset. Back to you, Bob.

title: Rules for the Treehouse Hotel
text:
Welcome to the Treehouse Hotel, the tallest hotel in the jungle! To keep everyone happy, please follow these rules.

Our elevator is a basket on a rope. Please ride it {adverb} and keep your {body part} inside at all times. Breakfast is served on the top branch at eight o'clock. Today we are having fresh mangoes and {plural noun}. Please do not share your food with the monkeys. They will {verb} on your table if you do.

Quiet time starts after dinner. Please do not {verb} in the hallways. The sloth in Room 4 has been trying to fall asleep since {noun} Day. Every room has a {adjective} hammock and a clean {noun}. If you need anything, ring the bell and a parrot will help you.

If you see a snake in your room, do not worry. His name is Steve, and he is just looking for his {color} hat. Thank you for staying with us! We hope your visit is {adjective}.

title: Toucan's Famous Fruit Salad
text:
Tilly the Toucan makes the best fruit salad in the jungle. Here is her secret recipe.

You will need two bananas, one mango, a bowl of berries, and a {adjective} coconut. You will also need {number} {plural noun}, but only the fresh ones. First, ask a monkey to help you {verb} the bananas. Monkeys are very good at this. Then cut the mango into the shape of a {noun}.

Next, put all the fruit into a big bowl and stir it {adverb} with your beak. If you do not have a beak, a spoon is fine. Now add a sprinkle of {food} on top. Tilly says this makes the salad taste {adjective}.

Finally, let the salad sit in the sun while you are {verb ending in ing}. Serve it to your friends and wait for them to say, "{exclamation}!"

title: Talking with a Sloth
text:
Our reporter, Jada, spent the whole day with Sid the Sloth. It took a while.

Jada: Hello, Sid! What does a normal day look like for you?
Sid: I wake up at noon. Then I hang upside down and think about {plural noun}. After that, I take a nap.
Jada: What is your favorite food?
Sid: Leaves, mostly. But on my birthday I have a {adjective} cake made of {food}.

Jada: Do you ever hurry?
Sid: Once. I heard someone was giving away free {plural noun}, so I moved {adverb}. It only took me {number} hours to get there.
Jada: What do you do for fun?
Sid: I like {verb ending in ing} with my best friend, a turtle named Gus. Someday we hope to {verb} together.

Jada: Thank you, Sid. Anything else for our readers?
Sid: Yes. Slow down and take time to {verb}. And always keep a {noun} in your fur.

title: Help Wanted: Jungle Tour Guide
text:
Help wanted! Jungle Fun Tours is looking for a new tour guide.

You must love animals, walking, and {plural noun}. You must be able to {verb} while carrying a big backpack. It also helps if you are {adjective} in the morning. Every day, you will lead visitors down the jungle trail. You will point out the parrots, the frogs, and the famous dancing {noun}. When visitors get tired, you will cheer them up by {verb ending in ing}.

The best part of this job is lunch by the waterfall. The hardest part is the monkeys. They like to grab your hat and your {noun}. Just say "{silly word}" {adverb}, and they will give them back.

You get one day off each week and a free {color} shirt. Our last guide loved this job so much that she {past tense verb} every single day. To apply, send us a drawing of yourself next to a {noun}.

title: The Jungle Talent Show
text:
Attention, all jungle animals! The Jungle Talent Show is this Saturday at the Big Rock by the river. Everyone is invited. The show will start when the sun is high and the frogs stop {verb ending in ing}. Please bring a blanket and a {noun} to sit on.

Here are some of the acts. The Monkey Brothers will {verb} on one hand while eating bananas. Lola the Leopard will sing a {adjective} song about {plural noun}. Then the elephant will play the trumpet with her {body part}.

The judges this year are an owl, a tortoise, and a very {adjective} anteater. The winner gets a golden coconut and {number} {plural noun}.

Snacks will be sold by the parrots. Please pay {adverb}, and do not let the parrots count the money. Last year they {past tense verb} and nobody knew how much anything cost. See you there!

title: A Letter from the River Boat
text:
Dear Grandpa,

I am writing to you from a boat on the jungle river. Captain Diaz lets me steer for {number} minutes every afternoon. Yesterday I steered us right into a {noun}, but nobody minded. The river is wide and brown and very {adjective}. Pink dolphins swim next to our boat. When I wave, they {past tense verb} and splash me with water.

Every night we eat dinner on the deck. The cook makes rice, beans, and a soup made of {plural noun}. Tonight a curious monkey climbed aboard and tried to {verb} with our spoons.

My favorite thing is falling asleep in my hammock while the frogs sing. They sound like {plural noun} {verb ending in ing} in the rain. I will bring you back a {adjective} surprise. Please tell the cat I said "{exclamation}!"

Love,
Maya
